summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY. I write firmware in bare-metal C on ARM Cortex-M4, programming GPIO, timer, ADC, and I2C peripherals directly at the register level, and have built both interrupt-driven and FreeRTOS-scheduled control loops on STM32. My work sits at the hardware/firmware interface: hand-written low-level drivers, multi-sensor I2C buses, UART bring-up, and system-level debugging to root-cause integration failures.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with a Raspberry Pi and an HC-05 Bluetooth link, translating 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands.

Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; root-caused sensor jitter at the hardware/firmware interface and resolved it through software calibration and resolution tuning.
Architected a Mixed Reality headset concept using real-time chroma keying without a green screen; produced full claims documentation and BOM through to productization.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Led a 25-member cross-functional team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and firmware integration end to end.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor (ARM Cortex-M4)
bullets: Programmed Cortex-M4 peripherals directly in bare-metal C at the register level (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); held the image to 3.68 KB Flash and 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate.
Hand-wrote a low-level I2C device driver and implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions with interrupt-driven sample capture.
Verified timing and peripheral behavior in Proteus before hardware bring-up.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret (STM32 + NVIDIA Jetson)
bullets: Implemented multi-servo PWM control on STM32 with interrupt-driven UART command parsing and a user override path.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination and scheduling; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing over I2C with OLED distance visualization.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) - M.S. Capstone, RIT
bullets: Root-caused 11 hardware/firmware integration failures including servo brown-out and stale-frame capture; achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end latency.
Bridged an embedded Linux host (Jetson) to an Arduino MCU over USB serial, driving five servos and two VL53L0X ToF sensors multiplexed on a shared I2C bus through a TCA9548A.
Implemented two-link inverse kinematics in C++ on the MCU with a 25 mm ToF-triggered contact gate for grasp closure.
